page: Microsoft Azure E8ps_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the EPSv5 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs powered by an Ampere Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The architecture is arm64 with 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. No local storage is bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable, and it does not include GPU hardware.

In benchmark evaluations, the E8ps_v5 demonstrates average performance across several compute and memory metrics. Stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests place the instance in the average tier, with scores of 1822.39 and 14507.4 respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 565.27 GB/sec and a large block uncached write speed of 43.18 GB/sec. However, the instance exhibits weaker performance in specific areas, such as single-threaded bzip3 decompression and Passmark CPU encryption tests, which fall into the poor and weak categories.

From a workload perspective, the high memory density makes this instance suitable for memory-intensive applications that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. It performs reliably in database operations, showing average performance in Passmark database tests and achieving 11.24 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. It is also capable of handling static web serving at 10.41 GB/sec. The ARM-based architecture provides a cost-efficient profile for memory-optimized workloads, though it is less suited for heavy cryptographic tasks or large-scale LLM inference.
